body:
I'm not sure that `buffer_get_data_async()` makes sense on a local rendering device since you have to sync anyway. It should probably just throw an error when you try to use it with anything other than the main rendering device

For clarity, `buffer_get_data_async()` allows you to avoid syncronizing the RenderingDevice when you want to grab data. This can have a major impact on frame rate since the RenderingDevice can queue up a couple of frames in advance. 

When using a local rendering device, everything runs async compared to the main rendering device. There are no frames, you control the operation of the RD with submit and sync manually. 

`buffer_get_data_async()` waits for all frames in the queue to complete before it calls the callback the data. But there are no frames queued up when using a local rendering device!

_edit: As I wrote that I realized that the system is waiting for the next frame, that's easy enough to manufacture, just give it another frame to work with! The following code works:_

```gdscript
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	time_waited += delta
	if ran_compute and time_waited >= WAITING_TIME_SECONDS:
		
		var sync_time = Time.get_ticks_msec()
		rd.sync() # <-------- Notice the sync here
		if ran_compute == "async":
			# If running after sync the callback is never called
			rd.buffer_get_data_async(buffers[0], extract_done)
			rd.submit() # <-------- now submit a frame so the callback is triggered
			rd.sync()
		if ran_compute == "sync":
			extract_done(rd.buffer_get_data(buffers[0]))
		ran_compute = null
		print("buffer_get_data blocked for: ", Time.get_ticks_msec() - sync_time, "ms")
```

_I guess we could add a fast path to `buffer_get_data_async()` to simply return immediately if called from a local rendering device. But, for the reasons I explained above, that would be no better than just using `buffer_get_data()` in this case. In summary, there is no reason to use `buffer_get_data_async()` in this case, it won't help your performance at all_

Thank you for this detailed answer!

For the `buffer_get_data_async` I guess the documentation should be made clearer or it should indeed raise an error when calling from a local rd.

I expected the method to let the GPU render frames while I was fetching the data generated with the local rendering device. I am not very familiar with graphics programming so I do not know if that makes sense. Do you know if there is a way to achieve that with godot? As `sync` and `buffer_get_data` cannot be called from another thread than the main one, the game freezes when pulling large data from the GPU. This can be experienced in my demo project when `DIM` is high enough.

Yep, just create your local RD on a different thread and do everything on a separate thread, then none of the operations will block the main thread.

Thank you for your response. I'm wondering whether I need to create the local RenderingDevice and execute compute shader rendering within the same thread. Specifically:

Can I create the RD in one child thread and submit/sync in another child thread?

More importantly, does creating a new RenderingDevice instance for each compute shader execution incur significant performance overhead?

If there's no substantial performance penalty, then it would be acceptable to perform all steps (from RD creation to sync()) within a single thread per execution.

I'd appreciate any insights about threading best practices with RenderingDevice in compute shader workflows.

> Thank you for your response. I'm wondering whether I need to create the local RenderingDevice and execute compute shader rendering within the same thread. Specifically:
> 
> Can I create the RD in one child thread and submit/sync in another child thread?

No, you must interact with the RD on the same thread you used to create it.

> More importantly, does creating a new RenderingDevice instance for each compute shader execution incur significant performance overhead?

Yes this would incur overhead and is not necessary. Not only will it harm performance, you will be wasting a lot of VRAM and RAM. 

> If there's no substantial performance penalty, then it would be acceptable to perform all steps (from RD creation to sync()) within a single thread per execution.

Initializing a local RD can take over a second on some devices due to driver/OS behaviour. You really should not do it at run time. 

> I'd appreciate any insights about threading best practices with RenderingDevice in compute shader workflows.

Don't forget, all your RD tasks are going to run on the same GPU and will be competing for resources. Having one local RD makes sense as you can use it to fill gaps in the normal rendering process on the global RD. But having more than one just means they will be fighting each other for GPU time. You would be better off scheduling the work yourself and running it on the singular local RD.

Thank you for your answer! Regarding the local RenderingDevice, I still have one question:

Is there currently any way in Godot to allow the main RenderingDevice to directly use data from a local RenderingDevice?

For example:

Can a texture output by a Compute Shader in a local RenderingDevice be used as a shader parameter for rendering in the main RenderingDevice?

Or must I read the Compute Shader results from the local RenderingDevice back to the CPU and then transfer them to the GPU again?

I’m trying to avoid the performance cost of GPU→CPU→GPU data transfers.

> Is there currently any way in Godot to allow the main RenderingDevice to directly use data from a local RenderingDevice?

No, there is no way. If you need the data to be on the global rendering device, then you should use the global rendering device instead of a local rendering device.

> Yep, just create your local RD on a different thread and do everything on a separate thread, then none of the operations will block the main thread.

I have this exact setup, but calling sync() on the rendering-device will still cause my main thread to freeze for a short time.
Also the documentation says:
>Forces a synchronization between the CPU and GPU, which may be required in certain cases. Only call this when needed, as CPU-GPU synchronization has a performance cost

But what is the alternative? What could be reasons why sync() still causes my main thread to stutter?

It could be nice to add this to the doc https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/shaders/compute_shaders.html

It does not mention a thread (as far as I know), and I think it's the first time I've seen someone mention this

Maybe it's me, but I think threading it's a rare thing to do, since you usually need the main thread data, so people might not notice they can do this

It is documented in the server:
> Creates a RenderingDevice that can be used to do draw and compute operations on a separate thread. Cannot draw to the screen nor share data with the global RenderingDevice.

I knew it was, I was suggesting to suggest it in the main documentation

It's using a local device too, but not a thread, and it does not share data with the main rendering device

It's not for me, now that I know it, I could open the issue in the documentation repo 🤷‍♂️
